newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - S.Africa May PPI seen improving.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - S.Africa May PPI seen improving.

text.p: South African producer inflation is expected to have improved in May as a stronger rand and slowing economy curb prices at the producer level, economists said on Friday.
The figure, due for release next Thursday at 0900 GMT, is expected to benefit from a dip in imported inflationary pressures as the perkier currency puts the brake on the price of foreign goods.

A Reuters consensus poll of eight economists predicted the overall producer price index would rise 0.8 percent month-on-month or 8.4 percent year-on-year after April's 0.4 percent and 8.8 percent rise.
Forecasts ranged from 8.1 to 8.9 percent year-on-year.
Economists said imported inflation was trending downwards against a year ago, especially after a dip in international oil prices.
"We had a strong rand and our May imports were relatively cheap," said Hania Farhan, economist at FBC Merchant Bank.

Inflation at the local level would also be dampened by the slowing economy and a falling trend in food prices, all of which was leading to increasing speculation on interest rate cuts later in the year.
"It is not one single factor. It is an overall mix of an economic slowdown, a stronger rand and easing food prices," said Julia Roy, treasury economist at Rand Merchant Bank.
Economists noted that May was a high survey month which could prod the month-on-month rate up, while the year-on-year rate would be subued by the fact that May 1996 had a high base effect.
Having widely predicted that April would see a turnaround in inflation figures, economists were predicting a steady downward trend over the next few months.
"Going from here over the next few months or so we will see it fairly steady around 8.5 percent and then have a big dip off near the end of the year," Nedcor group economist Dennis Dykes said.
